dedupe_keys.name: fao disasters in agriculture damage and loss interactive 2008 2018

description: This FAO interactive presents the damage and losses that disasters caused to crop and livestock production in least developed and low to middle income countries from 2008 to 2018, as a summary of FAO's report The impact of disasters and crises on agriculture and food security 2021. It gives production losses by region, such as 49 billion US dollars in Asia, 30 billion in sub-Saharan and North Africa, 29 billion in Latin America and the Caribbean and 8.7 billion in Caribbean small island states, and ranks hazards: drought caused over 34% of losses, 37 billion dollars, with 82% of drought impact falling on agriculture, followed by floods at 21 billion dollars, or 19%, and storms. It also covers nutritional effects and desert locusts, the 2020 hurricane season and COVID-19. It is produced by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). Coverage is global across developing countries. The interactive page is free, with figures linked to the earlier FAO damage and loss publication and the full 2021 report downloadable through its DOI. Caveats: estimates rely on FAO's damage and loss method and national reporting, small unreported disasters are hard to capture, and no licence is stated on the page. For simulation it gives loss rates by hazard for agricultural exposure and resilience models and baselines for climate adaptation studies. It is related to the FAO Locust Watch record in this catalogue.
